quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Move back to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Move back to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move back to your lane when you have enough space between you and the car you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, move back to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a:

options.text: Solid red light.
Stop sign.
Yield sign.
Caution sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer going 55 mph could take up to ____ to stop.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need about 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: Your body removes about:

options.text: Three alcoholic drinks an hour.
One alcoholic drink an hour.
Two alcoholic drinks an hour.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink an hour.
questions.explanation: The average person's body processes about one drink per hour. How impaired you become depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink it, your weight, how much you have eaten, and your health.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow, you should:

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming cars and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. You should:

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can:

options.text: Cause your engine to use too much oil.
Mean your car needs a tune-up sooner.
Make you sleepy while driving.
Start fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust system are dangerous and can cause drowsiness while you drive.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads divided by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:

options.text: Traffic lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
How the road surface is.

questions.correctAnswerText: How the road surface is.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how well you can stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or in poor condition to stay in control. Driving too fast on slippery roads makes it hard to stop and is dangerous.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Other drivers can follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the other lane.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to come on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the other lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full lane. Make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane before you pass a motorcycle on the left.

questions.question: Your vehicle stops more slowly when stopping:

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more distance to stop on wet or icy roads. It also needs more distance on roads with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop faster than cars.
Do not need more room to turn than cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Stay out of these areas. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more room to turn and stop than cars.

questions.question: A speed limit sign for curves or turns:

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Has a triangular shape.
Is blue with black letters.
Shows a recommended speed for that curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for that curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Warning signs for curves and turns often show a recommended speed. Even if you feel safe going faster in good weather, you should never go faster in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line. You know right away that:

options.text: It is a two-way road.
It is a one-way road.
The road is under repair.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Broken yellow lines can be crossed to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: On a one-way street, an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you. You must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may come from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopping:

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, there is less chance of a collision.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. You should:

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another vehicle hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: It is important to watch for motorcycles because:

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can easily hide in a car's blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is and how fast it is going. Always be alert and careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Maintain a constant speed throughout the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve. Speed up gradually as you exit. Speeding up when entering a curve makes your car hard to control.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spots by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Using the outside rearview mirror.
Using both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: You are driving and hear a siren. You cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down. Don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but cannot see where the emergency vehicle is, pull over to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you are sure the vehicle is not coming toward you.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing without flashing warning signals or crossing gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any train before crossing railroad tracks. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Never shift gears while crossing because your car could stall.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are a series of curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road has three or more curves coming up.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You may cross a solid yellow line only when turning.

questions.question: When parking your vehicle downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels sharply to the right. If your car rolls downhill, it will roll toward the side of the road and away from traffic.

questions.question: If you are turning onto a street with more than one lane traveling in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
Turn into the middle lane.
Turn into any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your direction, turn into the lane that is closest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What is a "No zone?"

options.text: A designated no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot of a large vehicle
An area designated for motor vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot of a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are the blind spots around large trucks and vehicles where smaller cars cannot be seen. Avoid staying in these areas.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: Your car is faster than the bicycle.
Bicycles always have the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you move out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle. The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road. Always drive carefully around bicycles.

questions.question: Why should drivers watch carefully for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They always have the right-of-way.
They do not have mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians are smaller than cars and harder to spot. Many crashes happen because drivers did not see them. They are also faster or have weaker lights. Always look carefully for these road users.

questions.question: In Idaho, when can you pass a vehicle in an intersection?

options.text: Never.
When a dashed yellow line goes through the intersection.
When both a dashed yellow line and a solid yellow line go through the intersection.
When there are no road markings in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a dashed yellow line goes through the intersection.
questions.explanation: You can pass in an intersection if a dashed yellow line continues through it. You cannot pass if there are no markings or if there is a solid yellow line next to a dashed yellow line.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too hard in the other direction.
Turn toward the traffic.
Turn the wheel in the direction the car is skidding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheel in the direction the car is skidding.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if your car skids. Steer the wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge ahead.
A lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.
Industrial area.
Highway entrance ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is getting narrower.
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. It is diamond-shaped with black text on yellow. It tells you that the right lane is ending or that the road will get narrower ahead.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic going in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It causes hearing loss.
It pollutes the air.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It makes the engine run poorly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your car. A leak lets these gases enter the cabin. Fix any exhaust leaks right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has rained for over an hour.
The day after rain.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery at the start of a rainstorm. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. This is worse in hot weather because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: What is important to do before turning left?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Let oncoming cars go first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for the other traffic light to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming cars go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep hill going down ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill going down ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead.
